operations.title: Entry 1211 — The Endpoint Vanishing Period Is Regular and Nonzero
operations.summary: At K0=0 the substitution z=-K2 t/K4 reduces the local form dz/sqrt(P) to -dt/(sqrt(K4)sqrt(-t(1-t))); the closed vanishing period is 2 pi i/sqrt(K4), independent of K2. The infinity endpoint gives 2 pi i/sqrt(K0). Thus the local Gysin map to the odd normalization costalk has rank one, while physical BD-chain activation remains unproved.

operations.title: Benincasa reports nonzero regular endpoint vanishing periods
operations.body: Entry 1211 computes the transverse endpoint periods exactly. At K0=0, z=-K2 t/K4 gives ∮dz/y=±2πi/sqrt(K4); at K4=0, xi=-K2 t/K0 gives ±2πi/sqrt(K0). K2 cancels, so the period has valuation zero and the local Gysin map onto Entry 1210's odd normalization costalk is rank one. This remains a local coefficient statement: no global BD relative-chain activation is asserted. Next is the ordered projective-overlap/Čech sign.
